channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Young People Don't Believe in 'American Dream': Kevin Gordon
item.description: Kevin Gordon, head of macro research & strategy at Schwab Center for Financial Research, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Jerry Maguire’ Inspiration on Lakers, Sports Valuations
item.description: Leigh Steinberg, legendary sports agent and founder of the Leigh Steinberg Foundation, spoke about the unprecedented valuations in the sports industry, highlighting the ongoing Los Angeles Lakers sale currently valued at $12.5 billion. He emphasized the dramatic increase in franchise values over the decades, noting that when he started in 1976, NFL expansion teams were purchased for $16.5 million, compared to recent sales reaching into the billions. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Boxing Legend Mike Tyson on Career, Sugar Factory Launch
item.description: Former Heavyweight Champion Mike Tyson discussed his new business venture partnering with Sugar Factory to produce high-protein sliders available in grocery stores. Tyson emphasized the health benefits of these sliders compared to typical frozen options that often contain unhealthy seed oils and excessive grams of fat. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthony Bourdain, 'A Moveable Feast': Must-Read Books
item.description: Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene discuss their must-read book on this week's edition of "Bloomberg Money." They discuss "Kitchen Confidential: Adventures in the Culinary Underbelly" by Anthony Bourdain and "The Greater Journey: Americans in Paris" by David McCullough. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Citadel Offloads Risk From Situational Awareness
item.description: Ken Griffin's Citadel has offloaded more than 80% of the aggregate risk associated with the Situational Awareness stock portfolio it acquired from the embattled AI hedge fund. Citadel struck a deal last month to buy stocks from the fund led by Leopold Aschenbrenner. Bloomberg's Hema Parmar reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Goldman's Struyven: Hedge Crude's Swings with Diesel
item.description: Daan Struyven, Goldman Sachs Co-Head of Global Commodities Research, discussed the market reaction to potential new US sanctions on Iran during a live financial news segment. He noted that oil prices experienced only a modest increase following the announcement, largely because the existing blockade on Iranian ports and oil exports is already restricting Iranian oil from reaching the market. He speaks with Romaine Bostick & Sally Bakewell on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hobbies Are Winning the Battle for Americans’ Paychecks
item.description: Bloomberg's Julia Franzares joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how consumers of all ages are making more room for pastimes in their budget, with hobbyists willing to cut elsewhere or dip into their savings to fund their hobbies. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Young Americans Living In 'Treat Economy': Kevin Gordon
item.description: Kevin Gordon, head of macro research & strategy at Schwab Center for Financial Research, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss how young Americans are 'treating' themselves as the typical American Dream is harder to achieve. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Millennials Feel Good About Their Finances, the Data Show Why
item.description: Bloomberg's Sarah Foster joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." Almost half of US millennials say their financial situation has improved from five years ago. That compares with 43% of Generation X and 40% of baby boomers who say the same. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Parents Spend $95K on Gap Years to Give Their Kids an Edge
item.description: Bloomberg's Sarah Foster joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." Gap years are becoming more appealing as families question whether a college degree alone is enough to stand out, with some programs costing more than a year of tuition. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Austerity Might Happen In Ugly Way: Rebecca Patterson
item.description: Rebecca Patterson, senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations and former chief investment strategist at Bridgewater Associates, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Something Has To Give' On US Fiscal Policy: Patterson
item.description: Rebecca Patterson, senior fellow at the Council on Foreign Relations and former chief investment strategist at Bridgewater Associates, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." Total US public debt surpassed $40 trillion for the first time, and has now surged by a third in less than five years, as US lawmakers continue to shrug off calls to contend with historically wide fiscal deficits. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bond Market Swings Affect Your Savings, Investments
item.description: Bloomberg's Nikki Waller and David Gura join Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." The Treasury surprised traders this week with its plan to buy back more debt. Long-dated yields plunged on Wednesday in response to the news, only to rebound the next day. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Moderna Soars 129% for the Week | Closing Bell
item.description: Comprehensive cross-platform coverage of the U.S. market close on Bloomberg Television, Bloomberg Radio, and YouTube with Romaine Bostick, Sally Bakewell, Carol Massar and Emily Graffeo. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Yields Soar, AI Pushback, Playing Politics: Roundtable
item.description: Bloomberg's Nikki Waller, Sarah Frier, and David Gura join Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss the whiplash in the US Treasury market this week and how it impacts personal finance and politics. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hedge Funds Cut Bearish Bets on European Diesel to Two-Year Low
item.description: Hedge funds slashed short-only positions on European diesel to the lowest in over two years while stacking up fresh bullish wagers, a sign that traders anticipate that a historic fuels crunch will stretch on.
item.dc:creator: Will Kubzansky

item.title: Bessent’s Bond Maneuvers Giving Global Debasement Trade New Life
item.description: Scott Bessent’s bid to tame US borrowing costs knocked down long-term yields for barely a day. The more lasting market signal: the dollar weakened while gold and Bitcoin rallied, reinforcing a debasement trade fueled by swelling US deficits and concerns over the direction of US economic policy.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie, Denitsa Tsekova and Isabelle Lee

item.title: SEC Accuses Ex-BofA Senior Banker Satsky of Insider Trading
item.description: Former senior Bank of America Corp. investment banker Jason Satsky passed on confidential information about a deal to a friend who made $18.5 million in illegal profits, according to the US Securities and Exchange Commission.
item.dc:creator: Nicola M White and Ava Benny-Morrison

item.title: Wild Weather Sends Crop Prices Rising in Risk to China Trade
item.description: Extreme weather is trimming US harvests and boosting prices for farmers just as top commodities importer China is increasing soybean purchases to meet a commitment struck between the two nations’ leaders.
item.dc:creator: Michael Hirtzer and Erin Ailworth

item.title: US Stocks End Week on Up Note, Nasdaq 100 Snaps Five-Day Slump
item.description: US stocks rose on Friday, finishing the week on an upbeat note that saw the Nasdaq 100 end a five-day losing streak as data revealed bustling business activity and Bitcoin soared.
item.dc:creator: Emily Forgash
